ch25.d.diel: Material filling the gap and its dielectric constant $\kappa$
ch25.d.source: Battery connected ($V$ fixed) or disconnected after charging ($Q$ fixed)
ch25.goal.C: Capacitance depends only on geometry and material: $C = \kappa\varepsilon_0 A/d$
ch25.goal.U: The energy of a capacitor is stored in the field between the plates: $U = \frac{1}{2}CV^2 = Q^2/2C$
ch25.obs.on: Battery connected ($V$ fixed): inserting a dielectric multiplies $C$ and $Q$ by $\kappa$, leaves $E$ unchanged, and raises $U$ by $\kappa$
ch25.obs.off: Battery disconnected ($Q$ fixed): inserting a dielectric divides $V$ and $E$ by $\kappa$ and lowers $U$ by $\kappa$
ch25.obs.gauss: Induced charge on the dielectric faces screens part of the plate charge, so fewer field lines cross the gap
ch25.obs.pull: Disconnected, a wider gap raises $V$ and $U$: the work done pulling the plates apart is stored
ch25.assume.ref: Reference state $X_0$: area 100 cm², gap 1 mm, empty gap, $V_0$ = 12 V. Disconnected means charged in the reference state, then disconnected
ch25.assume.edge: Edge effects neglected (uniform field between the plates); the dielectric fills the whole gap
ch25.assume.draw: The drawn gap is exaggerated relative to the plate size. Field lines are linear in $E$ (5 across the reference plate at $E_0$); below one line a single shorter arrow, its length proportional to $E$. Free charge is linear in $\sigma$ on the same scale; when the symbols would not fit, one symbol stands for several charges, shown by the key $\oplus \times n$ above the plate. Induced charge cancels the fraction $1 - 1/\kappa$ of the free charge
